item.title: The Strength–Ductility Frontier: Just-in-Time Hardening, the Limits of Uniform Deformation, and a Design Rule for Strong, Ductile Alloys

A metal can begin to neck with substantial hardening still in reserve. We separate the size of that reserve from the schedule that delivers it. For homogeneous, rate-independent tension with reserve equal to yield stress, the sharp limits for positive exponential relaxation, non-increasing hardening and the marginal ideal are 0.232, 0.500 and 0.693 true plastic strain. A single rate is optimal over the entire relaxing class, yet even that rate needs more than e times the marginal reserve at equal nonzero strain below one. The penalty belongs to exponential relaxation, not to a falling tangent alone. The inverse test gives two design quantities: the stress the mechanism must add and the hardening rate it must still supply at the target strain. Measured tensile endpoints can rule out a non-increasing tangent; three early stress readings can bound the first instability for positive, non-increasing, log-convex hardening. In 90 specimens from 22 series, 90 nominal lower bounds and 68 lower bounds tested throughout a ±0.5 MPa stress box lie below the sampled peak proxy. The prespecified SUS301L 5%-martensite onset window missed the observed optimum, separating that phase-marker rule from the mechanical timing law. A survey of 2,174 alloy-condition entries across three compilations yields an atlas of 805 scored tensile records. Among 300 records at or above 500 MPa yield, 2 or 15 cross a Voce-inferred headroom of 3% of shear modulus, depending on the elongation convention; the best-passive minimum gives 0 or 11 crossings. In the 796-record endpoint comparison, the inferred pre-peak stress rise is approximately flat against yield but declines relative to yield. A full-curve check found that the proxy overestimated scheduling efficiency by 31% in the two sheet alloys tested. The atlas ranks inferred requirements and flags cases for direct testing. The design studies turn the bounds into three decisions. For a conductive copper contact, we specify the particle hardening needed for 680 MPa proof stress and 12% uniform elongation at a same-state target of 75% IACS. In the separate rigid-plastic comparison at 680 MPa plastic onset, the same elongation calls for 258 MPa of relaxing reserve versus 81.6 MPa at marginal stability. For laminated-titanium, we predict where delaying transformation can cause an abrupt loss of uniform strain. For β cryogenic steel, a cylinder calculation shows that the grade order can reverse at unchanged phase-marker strains. Each result identifies what hardening the design needs and the measurement that would decide whether the material can supply it. Keywords: strength–ductility trade-off; diffuse necking; Considère criterion; dislocation retention; transformation-induced plasticity; moment problem; inverse materials design; copper conductors; metastable titanium; liquid-hydrogen tanks; rate-limited mechanisms; forming limits; energy absorption; temperature paths Published: 2026-11-23T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research) 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

The use of advanced numerical methods for the simulation and design of steel components and structures has increased rapidly in recent years. The response of elements experiencing large plastic deformations and even fracture can now be accurately captured. For such analyses, the full true stress-strain relationship of the material up to the fracture strain is required. While pre-necking stress-strain behaviour has been extensively studied, the post-necking behaviour remains less well defined and there are no standardised predictive models. This paper focuses on the post-necking true stress-strain behaviour of hot-rolled steels. Three alternative standardised true stress-strain models for use under any stress state are developed – a Nonlinear post-necking Model (NM), a Simplified Nonlinear post-necking Model (SNM) and a One-stage Nonlinear hardening Model (ONM). Empirical predictive equations for the key post-necking material properties, including the reference true fracture stress and strain, and the roundness of the post-necking true stress-strain curve are developed. The developed predictive equations were derived from a dataset comprising 256 standard tensile coupon tests on hot-rolled steels. Since post-necking behaviour cannot be obtained directly from experimental measurements, each coupon was first numerically simulated, and the key material parameters were extracted from the numerical results. The accuracy of the proposed equations was evaluated and shown to provide good predictive performance, demonstrating their applicability in facilitating the increasing use of advanced computational methods for the analysis and design of steel structures. The SNM formulation, together with the associated predictive equations, provides both high prediction accuracy and a simple functional form, while satisfying the Considère criterion and remaining compatible with existing pre-necking models. The SNM formulation has been accepted for inclusion in EN 1993–1–14, and is suitable, in conjunction with appropriate strain limits and partial factors, for use in both numerical design calculations and simulations. This paper presents a nonlocal non-associated plasticity framework for predicting plastic deformation and characterizing stress-state-dependent fracture forming limits of EN AW 6082 aluminum alloy sheets. A combined hardening law, together with the Drucker–Prager yield condition and a non-associated von Mises flow rule, is used to describe plastic behavior under large deformations. A plastic predictor–elastic corrector method is employed for the numerical implementation of the proposed nonlocal plasticity model. The main contribution of this work is the numerical implementation of an integral-based nonlocal plasticity formulation within the Abaqus finite-element framework, enabling the regularization of localized plastic deformation and stress-state variables relevant to ductile fracture. An explicit UEXTERNALDB-based approach is implemented in Abaqus together with a user-defined subroutine. The formulation enables the equivalent plastic strain and stress-state variables, including stress triaxiality and the Lode parameter, to be calculated nonlocally within a conventional finite-element framework, thereby reducing mesh dependency associated with strain localization. Nakajima tests with different specimen geometries are conducted to investigate the formability of thin aluminum alloy sheets. A modified stress-state-dependent, strain-based Bai–Wierzbicki (BW) ductile fracture model is employed to characterize fracture behavior. In contrast to the conventional forming-limit-curve approach, the fracture forming limit diagram is derived from the stress-state-dependent ductile fracture model. Digital image correlation is used to measure the strain fields during the Nakajima tests. The results demonstrate that the nonlocal plasticity formulation reduces mesh sensitivity associated with localized deformation and stress-state characterization, while the modified BW fracture criterion improves the description of stress-state-dependent fracture forming limits. By combining nonlocal regularization with an enhanced stress-state-dependent fracture criterion, the proposed framework provides a robust numerical basis for the analysis of fracture forming limits in sheet metals. Understanding the stress-state dependence of adiabatic shear band (ASB) initiation is essential for the modeling and design of high-strength steels used in extreme dynamic applications. In this study, the high strain-rate and failure behavior of Armox 500T are systematically investigated under proportional axisymmetric tension, compression, and compression-shear loading. Direct compression and split-tensile Hopkinson bar experiments are combined with inclined compression-shear specimens to isolate Lode-angle-dependent effects on strain localization, ductility, and ASB initiation. Full-field digital image correlation (DIC), together with optical, scanning, and transmission electron microscopy is used to correlate macroscopic mechanical response with microstructural evolution. The results reveal pronounced asymmetry in high strain-rate behavior. Dynamic tension exhibits enhanced strengthening (up to 12%) and sustained ductility, whereas dynamic compression loading results in over 50% embrittlement due to ASB formation. Furthermore, enhanced shear loading increases the propensity to ASB initation leading to severe embrittlement driven by intense shear localization along the plane of maximum shear. Microstructural analysis reveals that ASB initiation is an intrinsic material response and energy-absorbing mechanisms remain active following band formation. By correlating interrupted dynamic tests with in-situ strain measurements, an experimentally defined, microstructurally validated instability strain associated with stress-state dependent ASB initiation is identified. It is revealed that under dynamic loading, the equivalent instability and fracture strains decrease by over 50% with increasing shear loading from uniaxial compression. Steam generator tubes in pressurized water reactors may develop defects during long-term service, potentially leading to rupture. This study develops a ductile-fracture-based finite element framework for predicting the burst pressure of Alloy 690TT steam generator tubes containing axial through-wall cracks. The material response is described using the Johnson–Cook plasticity model coupled with a ductile damage model that accounts for stress triaxiality and the Lode parameter. Material parameters were calibrated using tensile test data obtained under different loading conditions and stress states. As the strain-rate effect on fracture strain was limited within the investigated range, strain-rate dependence was incorporated into the plasticity model but neglected in the damage model. The calibrated model was validated against tensile test results and subsequently applied to tubes containing axial through-wall cracks of different lengths. The predicted burst pressures agreed well with fracture-mechanics-based semi-empirical predictions and published experimental data, with maximum relative deviations of 2.6% and 4.0%, respectively. The predicted burst pressure decreased with increasing crack length, consistent with the reference results. The simulations also captured the progressive rupture process, from plastic deformation and damage initiation to damage evolution and final fracture. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for predicting the burst pressure of cracked Alloy 690TT steam generator tubes and supports their structural integrity assessment. item.title: Mechanical characterization and constitutive modelling of 8011-O aluminium alloy sheets for fin forming
item.description: 库内相似论文：Experimental characterization and constitutive modeling of an aluminum 7085-T711 alloy under large deformations at varying strain rates, stress states, and temperatures（相似度 0.730） 应变率效应: 可作为率项形式、率敏感性转折和动态试验技术的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对率区间、波形是否平衡、是否与准静态同一试样构型 摘要片段: Accurate representation of anisotropy, strain rate … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 塑性变形与硬化律: 可作为硬化律选型与颈缩后外推方案的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定应变范围、外推是否有独立验证、是否混用不同试样 摘要片段: The measurements showed pronounced directional variation … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 摘要方法线索: Johnson-Cook, Hill48 改进扩展线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 摘要方法线索: Johnson-Cook 采用方法线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: Accurate representation of anisotropy, strain rate sensitivity and fracture is needed to simulate the forming of thin aluminium fins. This study characterizes 8011-O aluminium alloy sheets with a thickness of 0.3 mm and develops material descriptions for fin forming. Room-temperature uniaxial tensile tests were conducted along seven in-plane orientations, and tests in the rolling direction covered strain rates from 10⁻⁴ to 10³ s⁻¹. Shear and notched tensile tests were used to characterize fracture under different stress states. The measurements showed pronounced directional variation in yield stress and plastic strain ratio, together with an increase in flow stress with strain rate. A modified Hill48 formulation was fitted to the directional yield stresses and plastic strain ratios, and a Johnson-Cook constitutive model with a polynomial strain rate coefficient was introduced. A Johnson-Cook fracture model was calibrated using the fracture tests. These material descriptions were then used in finite element simulations of fin piercing and flanging. The simulations identified localized thinning near the punch radius. Comparison with forming experiments gave a maximum relative error of 9.68% in the thinning ratio. Both the simulations and experiments showed fracture at a punch speed of 500 mm s⁻¹. The results provide a basis for assessing thickness variation and fracture during 8011-O aluminium fin forming. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Complex+plasticity+and+ductile+fracture+modeling+of+30CrMnSiNi2A+steel&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.rineng.2026.114280%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Today, structures must be designed effectively, which involves a large application of numerical simulations in addition to experiments. The presented work investigates high-strength steel 30CrMnSiNi2A tested at room temperature and quasi-static loading across a wide range of stress states, covering tension, compression and torsion, showing the insufficiency of classical metal plasticity to describe the observed material behavior. It is shown that neither a simple dependence on stress triaxiality nor a dependence on the normalized third invariant of deviatoric stress tensor could lead to an improvement in reproducing the measured responses. Therefore, complex plasticity is proposed considering the dependence on modified stress triaxiality. The new model better predicts the force and torque responses of specimens loaded in torsion and compression, reducing the mean absolute percentage error over the mentioned specimens by approximately 7 percentage points compared to the von Mises yield criterion. Furthermore, three uncoupled phenomenological ductile fracture criteria are calibrated and analyzed for practical application of the developed material model provided as an Abaqus user subroutine. However, the criteria have lower fidelity at compression stress state and low stress triaxialities where fracture data were missing, as it remains difficult to collect them for such ductile material. It can be used in industry and academia to simulate both manufacturing processes and operations of machine parts or products ranging from aerospace to defense. Titanium/steel bimetallic structures combine the high specific strength and excellent corrosion resistance of titanium alloys with the high ductility and low cost of stainless steels, offering broad application prospects in aerospace, nuclear energy, and marine engineering. However, direct joining is restricted by significant differences in their thermophysical properties and metallurgical compatibility, which readily lead to brittle Fe-Ti intermetallic phases and interfacial cracking. In this work, a TC4 alloy powder containing 8 wt.% Cu (TC4-8Cu) was used to fabricate a TC4-8Cu/316L bimetallic structure via electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF). A metallurgically bonded, crack-free interface was obtained, consisting of the TC4-8Cu matrix, a Cu-rich zone, an intermetallic compound (IMC) layer, and the 316L matrix. Cu preferentially reacted with Ti to form Ti 2 Cu near the interface, which consumed the available Ti, restricted Fe-Ti interdiffusion, and effectively suppressed the formation of continuous brittle Fe-Ti layers. Tensile tests revealed a distinct two-stage fracture process. At room temperature, the 316L side fractured first at a peak stress of 482 MPa, followed by load transfer to the titanium side, resulting in an ultimate tensile strength of 636 MPa. At 350°C, the fracture sequence reversed: the TC4-8Cu side failed first at 618 MPa, and the remaining 316L section sustained a load-transfer stress of 190 MPa. These results demonstrate that powder-composition design with Cu can regulate interfacial reactions and preserve structural integrity in EB-PBF-fabricated titanium/steel bimetallic structures. ABSTRACT This study investigates the low‐velocity impact response and damage evolution of fiber–metal hybrid sandwich (FMS) beams consisting of GFRP skins, embedded steel tooth plates, and polyurethane foam cores. The steel tooth plate is integrated with the GFRP layers, while the tooth elements penetrate into the foam core to provide additional through‐thickness mechanical constraint between the hybrid face sheet and the core. The effects of steel tooth plate reinforcement, impact energy, foam core density, and GFRP face‐sheet thickness on the impact response and failure mechanisms were studied. The results show that the hybrid face sheet significantly improved the impact resistance of the sandwich beams. Compared with conventional GFRP sandwich beams, the peak impact forces of the FMS beams increased by 31.2%, 48.4%, and 33.4% under impact energies of 22, 33, and 44 J, respectively. Increasing impact energy caused a progressive transition from elastic‐dominated indentation to local bending and interfacial damage. Foam‐core density strongly influenced the balance between deformation tolerance and local contact resistance: lower‐density cores exhibited progressive crushing and distributed bending deformation, whereas higher‐density cores showed greater contact resistance but a stronger tendency toward localized perforation. Increasing GFRP face‐sheet thickness improved local deformation resistance, but its effectiveness was strongly coupled with foam core density. An analytical model based on elastic–plastic foundation theory was developed to predict local bending and perforation damage of the hybrid face sheet. Deep-sea titanium-alloy pressure hulls subjected to underwater explosions experience successive shock-wave and bubble-pulsation loading, resulting in rapidly varying strain rates, severe local deformation and potential structural damage. Understanding the influence of rate-dependent fracture energy on damage evolution is therefore important for assessing their dynamic response and structural integrity. In this study, a strain-rate-dependent fracture-energy formulation was established for Ti-6Al-3Nb-2Zr-1Mo using compressive responses over a strain-rate range of 0.02–3670 s -1 . The effective fracture-dissipation energy density A f was determined, and its rate-dependent relationship was incorporated into an independent energy-based damage-evolution law following Johnson–Cook damage initiation. The applicability of the proposed formulation was validated through Charpy impact tests. The validated formulation was subsequently applied to a ring-stiffened cylindrical pressure hull using coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian simulations to investigate the effects of fracture-energy level and TNT mass on its dynamic response. The results show that the effective fracture-dissipation energy density A f exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on strain rate. The numerical Charpy impact responses agree with the experimental measurements within an acceptable error range for the principal global response measures, reproducing the overall load–displacement trend and post-peak softening behavior. Fracture energy primarily affects post-initiation deformation and energy dissipation, with its influence becoming particularly pronounced during the subsequent bubble-pulsation stage. In contrast, TNT mass affects both the initial shock-wave intensity and the subsequent bubble response. These findings provide a material-specific basis for assessing the dynamic damage response of titanium-alloy pressure hulls. From an engineering perspective, the rate dependence of effective fracture energy should be considered in near-field or severe underwater-explosion scenarios that involve local damage initiation, progressive softening, residual structural-integrity assessment or significant secondary damage induced by bubble pulsation. This paper evaluates gun-launch survivability of a critical ammunition component by comparing conventional elastic-plastic material models with Johnson–Cook (JC) strength models. Compressive JC models for 7075-T651 aluminum were developed using quasi-static and Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) compression tests over a range of strain rates and temperatures, with two post-processing methods used to extract JC constants. Finite element simulations in ABAQUS showed that JC models (tensile and compressive) consistently reduced the apparent margin of safety by ~6% relative to elastic-plastic analysis and altered the strain distribution within the critical component, providing insight into observed low-rate intermittent failures. The results indicated limited strain-rate sensitivity but non-trivial thermal softening behavior for this material, and demonstrated that improved calibration of the JC hardening parameters enhances representation of the gun-launch deformation state, motivating further refinement of the JC model. This study employed a Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) apparatus to conduct dynamic compression experiments on cylindrical specimens of as-rolled AZ31 magnesium alloy machined along directions at 0 o , 30 o , 45 o , 60 o , and 90 o to the rolling direction (RD), at temperatures of 25°C, 100°C, and 200°C under a strain rate of 1000s −1 . The effects of loading direction and temperature on the dynamic compressive mechanical behavior and microstructural evolution of the material were investigated. Combined analyses of true stress–true strain curves, Electron Back Scatter Diffraction(EBSD), Optical Microscopy (OM),and Transmission Electron Microscopy(TEM) revealed the mechanical responses, twinning behavior, and dislocation density variation patterns under different conditions.The results indicate that the true stress–true strain curves exhibit a typical “S” characteristic. {10 1 ¯ 2} tensile twinning and dislocation slip are the dominant deformation mechanisms . Schmid factor calculations show that pyramidal slip has the highest average SF values (0.39∼0.44), while basal slip (SF = 0.238∼0.302) is more difficult to activate. The loading direction significantly affects the twin volume fraction and peak stress，specimens compressed along the 90 o direction to RD exhibit the highest peak stress (297 MPa), the highest twin fraction (21.59%), and the highest dislocation density (3.00 × 10 16 m −2 ). With increasing deformation temperature, the peak stress decreases notably, and the fractions of both {10 1 ¯ 2} tensile twins and {10 1 ¯ 1}compression twins are reduced compared to those at room temperature, while for the 90 o sample,the geometrically necessary dislocation (GNDs) density increases to 4.01 × 10 16 m −2 at 100°C . TEM observations confirm the coexistence of , , and dislocations with{10 1 ¯ 2} tensile twins. This study provides key experimental evidence for engineering applications and numerical simulation of AZ31 magnesium alloy under impact loading. A three-dimensional hybrid framework is presented for ductile fracture of metals under large deformation. It couples ordinary state-based peridynamics (OSB-PD) with the Material Point Method (MPM). MPM carries the bulk plastic flow and avoids remeshing. OSB-PD is activated only where damage develops. It resolves crack initiation and growth. The PD region is not set in advance. It is created by a triaxiality-dependent criterion and follows the crack front. Plasticity in this region is written through bond extension states and corresponds to J 2 elastoplasticity. Bond failure uses an energy criterion adapted from peridynamic finite crack extension. It links elastic energy release to plastic dissipation. A blended force transfer joins the two descriptions. In a one-dimensional wave test, the relative L2 error is 1.30% and the reflected amplitude stays below 0.3%. A damage-gradient-based horizon scaling (DGHS) limits truncation errors near crack fronts. Bonds are symmetrized, so action and reaction stay balanced. Switching DGHS off delays the load drop and raises the dissipated energy by about 2%. The model is calibrated on one in-situ tension test of Q235B steel. The peak stress is 2.7% below the measured value. This is a calibration result, not an independent validation. With the same parameters, the model gives internal crack initiation and a cup-and-cone profile. It also predicts a mixed-mode crack path in a notched specimen. Grid and horizon effects are separated. The response converges for particle spacings of 0.025 mm or finer. A larger horizon delays failure. Validation rests on one material and one loading rate. Snow is a complex geomaterial whose macroscopic response is governed by density, temperature, and topology of its evolving microstructure. Its mechanical behavior spans elastic, plastic, viscous, and failure-dominated regimes, posing significant challenges for numerical methods intended to simulate large deformations, evolving free surfaces, and complex boundary interactions. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this work presents the first integration of a Modified Cam-Clay constitutive formulation for snow into a purely meshfree strong-form collocation framework based on the Generalized Finite Difference Method. The main methodological contribution is a numerical coupling that combines a global implicit mixed formulation for pressure and velocity with a constitutive return-mapping algorithm. The hydrostatic pressure contribution is obtained from a Poisson equation and subsequently corrected through the Modified Cam-Clay return-mapping procedure, while the deviatoric response is treated semi-implicitly using a numerical viscosity formulation. This partitioned treatment of the volumetric and deviatoric stress contributions enables stable simulations with comparatively large time steps, while producing smooth spatial pressure fields. As a result, interface forces on complex boundary geometries can be evaluated from these fields. Numerical results of this coupling illustrate the algorithmic stability of the framework, the effective imposition of boundary conditions, and the suitability of local spatial refinement. The feasibility of applying the framework to vehicle-snow interaction through rigid-body coupling is also illustrated. The presented formulation provides a numerical basis for future investigations of dynamic snow loading on vehicle structures. item.title: Effect of loading history in necking and fracture
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：Fracture of 1045 steel under complex loading history（相似度 0.790） 被相关论文引用：An incremental stress state dependent damage model for ductile failure prediction [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-016-0081-2] 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: The effect of Lode angle parameter, … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 延性断裂准则: 可作为断裂轨迹形式与起裂判据的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定试样组合、是否覆盖你的应力状态区间、有无独立验证试样 摘要片段: Similarly, a generalized asymmetric 3D empirical … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 The effect of Lode angle parameter, or the third deviatoric stress invariant, on plasticity and fracture is studied using flat-grooved transverse plane strain specimens. A generalized asymmetric plasticity model for isotropic materials with both pressure and Lode angle dependence is developed. Calibration method of the plasticity model is discussed in detail. Test results on 2024-T351 aluminum alloy confirmed the proposed plasticity model. Similarly, a generalized asymmetric 3D empirical fracture locus with six free parameters is proposed. The proposed fracture locus, which depends on both stress triaxiality (or pressure) and the Lode angle parameter, is calibrated using two types of methods: classical specimens under uniaxial testing, and the newly designed butterfly specimens under biaxial testing. Experimental results on 2024-T351 aluminum alloy, 1045 steel, and A710 steel validated the proposed 3D fracture locus. A concept of forming severity is introduced to study the loading history effect on metal forming limit diagram (FLD). Given the necking locus under proportional loading conditions, and using a non-linear accumulation rule of forming severity index, the proposed model well predicts the FLDs under different pre-loading conditions. As an extension of the ductile fracture locus defined and calibrated under proportional loading conditions, a new damage accumulation rule considering the loading history effect is proposed. The new model uses the accumulated difference between directions of the back stress tensor and the current stress tensor to describe the non-proportionality of a load path. Several types of tests with complex loading histories were designed and performed to study the loading history effect on ductile fracture. Extensive experimental studies on 1045 steel confirmed the proposed ductile fracture model. The proposed model is successfully applied to predict fracture of crushed prismatic tubes undergoing strain reversal. item.title: Fracture prediction in metal sheets
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：New ductile fracture criterion for prediction of fracture forming limit diagrams of sheet metals（相似度 0.776） 被相关论文引用：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: In the first part, the new … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 延性断裂准则: 可作为断裂轨迹形式与起裂判据的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定试样组合、是否覆盖你的应力状态区间、有无独立验证试样 摘要片段: In the first part, the new … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 One of the most important failure modes of thin-walled structures is fracture. Fracture is predominantly tensile in nature and, in most part, is operated by the physical mechanisms of void nucleation, growth, and linkage. For ductile sheet, fracture is preceded by necking. Prediction of necking which limits sheet metal formability is well established and has been developed over the past several decades. However, an in-depth understanding of the mechanical process inside the neck leading to sheet metal fracture is lacking. This is true for both static and high intensity, short duration loads. Furthermore, there is an ever increasing need to raise the safety envelope of existing protective structures against localized extreme loading. The present thesis addresses four parts of the many outstanding issues in sheet metal fracture. In the first part, the new Bao-Wierzbicki (BW) fracture criterion formulated in terms of the accumulated equivalent plastic strain with the stress triaxiality as a weighting function is considered. Using the equations of plane stress von-Mises plasticity and the strain-to-stress mapping procedure, the BW fracture criterion is transformed to the spaces of the principal tensile strains and stresses in a sheet and compared with experimental results for various materials. An extensive comparative study of the most widely used fracture criteria is then conducted. Weakly-textured magnesium (Mg) alloys often exhibit nominally isotropic stress–strain behavior with muted tension–compression asymmetry, making an isotropic plasticity assumption appear reasonable. Here, we assess the validity of that assumption for ductile damage governed by void growth and coalescence. The response of a nominally isotropic Mg alloy is represented using three constitutive descriptions: isotropic J2 plasticity, orthotropic HILL plasticity, and a mechanism-based multi-surface plasticity formulation. Finite-deformation finite-element simulations are performed on a porous periodic unit cell with fully periodic boundary conditions, subjected to constant macroscopic stress states corresponding to purely tensile loading and combined tension–shear loading. The results show that the damage response depends sensitively on the evolving distribution of deformation mechanisms around the void, which cannot be reproduced by isotropic matrix idealization. Importantly, the analysis suggests a subtle yet important role of these mechanisms, which extends beyond setting the net plastic anisotropy that can affect the predicted ductility.
